packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-19 -- unverified image-only reading (first reader)

Exposure: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or earlier reading of this packet. I did nothing beyond the reader rules (I created the scratch folder; listed only the packet directory's image names and dimensions with sips).

LAYOUT SURVEY (from overviews image-001 and image-004)
- image-001 (reduced overview, face A): two small separate parchment fragments side by side on black, scale bar right. Each roughly 6 x 8 cm by the scale. Left piece: a single column of small, dense, heavily abbreviated gothic text (approx. 20+ lines visible), with a ruled blank margin on the left carrying a later pencil/ink shelfmark-like note ("Stams ..."? with numbers -- modern, not read as text). Coloured initials/paraphs in blue and red within the column (blue at upper right edge, red near line 6-7, blue "D"-like initial mid-column, red paraph lower). Right piece: single column, text runs to a ruled right margin; blue and red initials/paraphs (blue at ~line 5, red at ~line 6, blue at ~line 9, blue near bottom); torn upper edge with what looks like a red mark at top; small holes.
- image-004 (reduced overview, face B, the reverse of the two pieces, reversed left-right relative to face A): left piece heavily stained, dense column text with red mark at left and lower left, paper/parchment patch at bottom. Right piece: text in the right half only, the left part abraded/stained (probably glue/pastedown damage); blue paraph near line 6, red mark at right margin.
- Tentative interpretation: strips cut from a small-format manuscript in a small textura/notular hand with dense Latin abbreviation, colored paraphs marking sections. No running titles visible; no interlinear glosses noticed at overview scale. Tiles: image-002/003 (face A pieces), image-005/006 (face B pieces), native resolution.

=== image-002.jpg (face A, left piece; native resolution; read via enlarged crops 002-top/002-mid/002-bot in rscratch/packet-19) ===
Observations: single column, ~27 lines visible on the tile (top line cut through, bottom line cut). Left margin ruled (horizontal rulings run into margin), blank except for a modern pencil note "Stams / STA Frag(?) / 37-2n(?)" -- modern archival note, not text. Right edge: text runs to the cut, words truncated. Hand: very small, angular, cursive-influenced gothic (notula-like) with extreme suspension/contraction; letters often reduced to minims. Coloured marks: line 4 a word underlined in blue ink ending in a blue paraph (open "D"-like mark); line 7 a word underlined in red with red paraph (red stroke continues into left margin); line ~14 a word underlined in blue with blue paraph; line ~22 underlined red with red paraph. These underlined + paraphed words look like section/lemma markers (tentative). Ink is abraded and the surface rough; legibility is low.

Honest assessment: I can read only isolated letter-groups. Readings below are very low confidence; most "words" are guesses at letter sequences, not secure Latin.

=== image-003.jpg (face A, right piece; native resolution; read via crops 003-a1, 003-a2, 003-a3, 003-b in rscratch/packet-19) ===
Observations: this tile shows the right piece of face A. It carries (a) the main column, 21 lines visible, written in the same small cursive gothic hand but more legible than image-002; (b) a ruled intercolumnar/margin space with a modern pencil note "Stams / STA / Frag. / 97-4n(?)" At the tile's far left edge are slivers of the other piece (not read here). Faint red stroke in left margin at ~line 13. Letters "a", "d", "q", "z" set off by points in lines 19-21 may be letter-labels used in an argument (tentative).
Overlap: none with image-002 except the left-edge slivers.

=== image-005.jpg (face B, right piece in image-004; native resolution; read via crops 005-top, 005-bot in rscratch/packet-19) ===
Observations: modern pencil note "Stams / STA Frag. / 97-?" written upside down in the lower-left blank area, so this face is the reverse of the right piece of face A (consistent with the left blank margin here being the back of the margin on image-003). A ruled vertical bounding line runs down the left side of the text block (with a faint green/grey line). One column, ~20 lines; the right half of the text block is badly abraded/stained (glue or pastedown damage) and mostly unreadable; the left half is clearer. A torn sliver/crease runs down through lines 12-16 at the left. Blue paraph mid-line at line 7; red paraph/initial at right edge on line 13 with red line-filler; at the bottom (line 20) a large ink-drawn initial (circular, O/Q-like, with blue touch at left) opening a new section. Letter-forms identical to face A (same hand).
Recurring word: "sol" (lines 2, 7, 15) -- reasonably secure. "illa"/"ille" (lines 7, 13, 14, 15) reasonably secure.

=== SUMMARY OF LIMITATIONS AND SELECTION ===
- Two small parchment pieces (~6 x 8 cm each), each written on both faces in the same small, heavily abbreviated cursive gothic hand, with red and blue paraphs and underlined words. Leaf was at least two-column (column b sliver on image-003; column-end sliver on image-006).
- Orientation: the LEFT piece of image-001 (= image-002) and the LEFT piece of image-004 (= image-006) are photographed upside down relative to the script; read them rotated 180 degrees. The right piece (image-003, image-005) is upright. My layout survey above described the left piece's colour marks as seen unrotated.
